markup:
To run a **refrigerator and a separate freezer** using a solar generator, I recommend a system with at least **2,000Wh (2kWh) of battery capacity and a 2,000W inverter**.

However, the right size depends on whether you want to run them for 12 hours, 24 hours, or continuously using solar panels.

## 1. Recommended solar generator size

Assuming a typical full-size household refrigerator and a separate chest or upright freezer:

| Backup duration | Battery capacity | Inverter power |
|---|---|---|
| 8–12 hours | 1,000–1,500Wh | 2,000W |
| 24 hours | 2,000–3,000Wh | 2,000W |
| 48 hours | 4,000–5,000Wh | 2,000W |
| 72 hours | 6,000–8,000Wh | 2,000W |
| Continuous with solar | 3,000–5,000Wh + panels | 2,000W+ |

These are planning estimates, not guarantees. Actual runtime depends on appliance efficiency, ambient temperature, door openings, and inverter losses.

## 2. How much electricity do they use?

Typical daily consumption:

| Appliance | Daily energy |
|---|---:|
| Full-size refrigerator | 1,000–2,000Wh |
| Separate freezer | 700–1,500Wh |
| **Combined** | **1,700–3,500Wh** |

For a reasonably efficient pair, let's assume **2,000Wh per day**.

A 3,000Wh solar generator with 85% usable AC energy provides approximately:

\[
3000 \times 0.85 = 2550Wh
\]

That gives you roughly **30 hours of operation** at 2,000Wh per day, without any solar charging.

## 3. How many solar panels do you need?

If you want to keep both appliances running indefinitely, solar panels must replace the electricity consumed each day.

<box gap={2}>
  <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Illustrative solar production with 4 peak sun-hours and 75% overall solar yield</text>
  {#each [{w:400,k:1.2},{w:600,k:1.8},{w:800,k:2.4},{w:1200,k:3.6}] as p}
    <row align="center" gap={3}>
      <box width="75px">
        <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{p.w}W</text>
      </box>
      <box flex="1" background="surface-tertiary" height="13px" radius="sm" clip>
        <box background="rgba(40,145,105,0.85)" width={`${p.k/3.6*100}%`} height="100%" radius="sm"/>
      </box>
      <box width="80px" align="end">
        <text size="sm" tabularNums>{p.k.toFixed(1)}kWh/day</text>
      </box>
    </row>
  {/each}
</box>

For a pair consuming 2kWh per day, **800–1,200W of solar panels** is a reasonable starting point, with extra capacity or grid backup for cloudy days and winter.

The generator must also support the panels' combined voltage and input wattage.

## 4. Example solar generators

  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity ref="turn893020product1" value={turn893020product1.title}/>**

    3,072Wh battery · 3,600W AC output

    <text weight="medium">{turn893020product1.displayed_price}</text>

    A good size for approximately one day of refrigerator and freezer backup, depending on consumption.
  </box>
</row>
<divider color="subtle"/>
<row gap={3} align="start">
  <AsyncImage ref="turn893020product5" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="132px" shop_eligible={true}/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity ref="turn893020product5" value={turn893020product5.title}/>**

    3,600Wh battery · 3,600W AC output

    <text weight="medium">{turn893020product5.displayed_price}</text>

    Larger battery with expandable capacity for longer outages.
  </box>
</row>

Remember that the inverter also needs enough **surge capacity** to start both compressors, especially if they start simultaneously.

Desired backup: ${duration}. Solar panels: ${solar}. Calculate recommended battery capacity, inverter surge power, panel wattage and estimated cost.`)}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>How long do you want backup power?</label>

        <radio value="24 hours">24 hours</radio>
        <radio value="48 hours">48 hours</radio>
        <radio value="72 hours">3 days</radio>

      </radio-group>
    </box>

    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What type of refrigerator?</label>

        <radio value="compact">Small or compact refrigerator</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>

      </radio-group>

        <radio value="unsure">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>

  </form>
